name: Lawn care
summary: Start a lawn care and snow removal business: your first 25 neighbors and partners, a price menu by yard size from real ranges, quotes from the curb and the right offer for the season where you live.
door_step3: I do the work and text you a photo
door_rule: Door hangers go on the door, never in or on a mailbox: putting unstamped flyers in a mailbox is a federal offense (18 U.S. Code 1725). Check your city rules on door to door flyers.

promises.first_25: 15 people you know and 10 local property managers, HOAs and agents, each with a message, plus door hangers with the offer that fits the season.
promises.offer: Your price menu by yard size, the first-clients ladder, a weekly plan, a snow contract and job math, on a one-page offer sheet.
promises.quote: Yard size, service and how often in; a quote, a text and an invoice out.
promises.keep: A thank-you, an honest review ask, your regular plan, a referral ask and a later check-in, each dated, plus review cards with your QR code.
promises.sample_one: A free demo for one street or one partner business: door hangers or a sample letter, a card to send and every message, saved to your Pipeline.
promises.reply: Paste what someone wrote back: what they meant, a short answer with one next step, and your Pipeline updated. A draft you send yourself.
promises.won: Log the yes, then everything for the job: the booking text, a prep text, a printable job sheet, the after-job text and the invoice.
promises.proof: One yard turned into proof: a result card, a before-and-after collage from your photos, a caption, an honest review ask and a case study once they say yes.
promises.next_25: The next 25 property managers, HOAs, agents and garden centers near you that are not in your Pipeline yet, with messages, saved for Do my day.
promises.ready: Look ready before you reach out: a one-page website, a Google profile kit and a flyer, all from your real prices.
promises.same_street: One customer's street turned into a route: door hangers with a neighbor price, a sheet for the 20 nearest homes and an intro ask for your customer.
promises.season_plan: Twelve months of offers for where you live: what to sell each month, who to reach, what to presell, with a calendar file and a one-page plan.

off_season.play: Sell snow contracts in September and October, then book spring cleanups and season mowing plans in February and March.

crowd.note: Off season November to March up north.

Don't take jobs across town. Same street first.
Don't apply fertilizer or weed killer for pay before checking your state's license rule.

licenses.disclaimer: General information, not legal advice. Rules differ by state, county and city: check your state and city.

items.what_to_check: City or county license; state registration for an LLC; DBA if you use a trade name.

sources.says: Licenses and permits depend on business activity and location; local governments set registration, licensing and permitting rules; research your own state, county and city; some licenses expire and must be renewed.
Get an EIN directly from the IRS online in minutes for free.

items.item: Pesticide applicator certification (weed control, insect control, some fertilizer products)
items.what_to_check: Many states require every commercial applicator to be certified, not only users of restricted use pesticides. Contact your state pesticide agency (usually the department of agriculture) before you sell weed or pest treatments.

sources.says: States, territories and tribes certify applicators; many states require all commercial applicators to be certified, stricter than federal rules; contact the state certifying agency and the state Pesticide Safety Education Program.
Sprayers for weed control or treatments: these services may require licensing depending on local regulations, so check before buying.

items.what_to_check: Thrown rocks, broken windows, damaged sprinkler heads and slip claims in winter.

sources.says: Lists common policies: general liability, product liability, professional liability, commercial property, home-based business insurance, and workers compensation; buy insurance required by law first, and taxes on employment insurance and workers compensation vary by state.
Reputable lawn care companies are usually licensed and insured to protect the customer if an accident or damage occurs.

items.what_to_check: A truck plus trailer rated 10,001 lb or more that crosses state lines is a commercial motor vehicle under federal rules (USDOT registration and safety rules). Some states have similar rules for in-state work; check your state DOT.

sources.says: Commercial motor vehicle: a vehicle used in interstate commerce with a gross vehicle or combination weight rating or weight of 10,001 pounds or more.

items.item: Small engine rules (California) and local leaf blower rules
items.what_to_check: California requires most newly made small off-road engines (mowers, leaf blowers) to be zero emission from model year 2024; existing compliant gas equipment can still be used. Some cities restrict gas leaf blowers or noise hours.

sources.says: Most newly manufactured small off-road engines such as leaf blowers and lawn mowers must be zero emission starting with model year 2024; Californians can keep operating current compliant gas equipment.

items.note: City noise and leaf blower rules vary; check your city code.

items.item: Snow work: sidewalk rules and written trigger depth
items.what_to_check: Many cities make property owners clear sidewalks, so clients care about timing. Put the trigger depth and response time in the written contract.

sources.says: Many cities require homeowners to clear the walkways bordering their property; each contract spells out the trigger amount and the timeframe for service.

steps: Before the season: written scope (mow, trim, edge, blow), frequency, price per visit, gate codes, pets, and the skip and rain-delay policy.
On arrival: walk the lawn and pick up sticks, toys, hoses and dog waste; note anything broken before you start.
Set mowing height for the grass type; follow the one-third rule (never cut more than a third of the blade at once).
Mow, then string trim around obstacles and fences, then edge along walks and driveway.
Blow clippings off concrete, porches and the street; clippings stay on the lawn unless bagging was agreed.
Close gates, take an after photo, note issues (bare spots, weeds, grubs) for an upsell later.
Invoice or charge the card on file the same day; ask happy clients for a review.

sources.says: Mowing, blowing clippings from concrete surfaces and edging the perimeter are typical mowing service features; follow the one-third rule.
Ask for a written agreement that details what is included, such as mowing, edge trimming and blowing clippings.
All-inclusive mow packages include mowing, weed-eating, edging and blowing, mulching or bagging clippings.

job_checklist.note: Pre-walk, photos and the notes for upsells are common practice, a judgment call.

seasonality.pattern: Lawn care peaks March to November and pairs with snow removal in winter: same truck, route, customers and skill.

sources.says: Lawn care peak Mar to Nov; season length is latitude. Lawn care pairs with snow removal (truck, route, customers, skill); a lawn customer who gets a note in October offering a snow contract costs nothing to acquire.

seasonality.pattern: Mowing season length depends on region: about 24 weeks in the Northeast, 26 in the Midwest, 34 in the West and Northwest, and 45 to 46 in the Southeast and Southwest.

sources.says: Weekly mowing season: Northeast about 24 weeks, Southeast about 45, Midwest about 26, Southwest about 46, West and Northwest about 34.

seasonality.pattern: Cool-season grasses grow most in spring and fall; warm-season grasses grow fastest in late spring and summer, so visit frequency changes through the year.

sources.says: Cool-season grasses grow more during early spring and fall, while warm-season grasses grow faster during late spring and summer.

seasonality.pattern: Fall is leaf cleanup season; spring brings cleanups, aeration and the first fertilizer rounds.

sources.says: Most people pay about $300 for a fall leaf clean-up on a 1/4 acre lawn.

seasonality.note: Spring timing is a judgment call.

seasonality.pattern: Snow contracts usually run November through March; sell them in September and October.

sources.says: Snow removal contracts last the entire snowy season, usually November through March.

seasonality.note: Selling window is a judgment call.
